newsitem.title: INDONESIA: ASEAN to call for Cambodia ceasefire - Alatas.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN to call for Cambodia ceasefire - Alatas.

text.p: ASEAN members will call on Tuesday for a ceasefire in Cambodia and foreign ministers of the seven-member group will meet this week to discuss the battered nation, Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said.
"ASEAN will issue a joint statement calling for a ceasefire," Alatas told reporters after meeting President Suharto.

He said the statement, due to be issued in Kuala Lumpur around mid-afternoon, would also express ASEAN's regret over the situation in Cambodia and call on all parties to settle their dispute through peaceful dialogue.
It would also call for protection of all foreign citizens in Cambodia.
The statement follows continued factional fighting between supporters of Cambodia's bitterly-opposed first and second prime ministers.

Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen took control of Phnom Penh in weekend fighting against supporters of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh. Factional fighting was also reported in northern Cambodia overnight Monday.

Diplomatic sources said the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), celebrating its 30th anniversary this year, would have to decide whether or not to admit Cambodia to the group as scheduled late this month.
Asked if the ministers at their special meeting would discuss Cambodia's membership, Alatas said they would "evaluate all aspects of the recent developments in Cambodia".
Malaysia is the current chairman of ASEAN, which also groups Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines and Brunei.
Another contentious country, Burma, and Laos are also due to join ASEAN at the same time at the annual regular foreign ministers' meeting in Kuala Lumpur at the end of July.
ASEAN sources said the group's secretary-general Ajit Singh was in Kuala Lumpur preparing for the formal session and was expected to attend the Thursday meeting.
